objects.title: Technological paradigms and technological trajectories
mechanisms: technological paradigms constrain search directions
technological trajectories organize cumulative improvement
objects.claim_boundary: Supports paradigm/trajectory structure, not deterministic timing or asset returns.

objects.title: Technological Revolutions and Financial Capital
mechanisms: installation and deployment phases
financial capital can precede productive deployment
turning points involve institutional adjustment
objects.claim_boundary: Used as an explanatory stage scaffold; does not authorize calendar forecasts of long-wave turning points.

objects.title: A Contribution to the Mathematical Theory of Epidemics
objects.source_locator: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 115(772):700-721
mechanisms: susceptible-infective-removed compartment dynamics
endogenous rise and decline of epidemics
objects.claim_boundary: Provides diffusion dynamics intuition; economic narratives are not asserted to be literally identical to disease transmission.

objects.title: Narrative Economics
objects.source_locator: NBER Working Paper 23075; AER 107(4):967-1004; uploaded w23075.pdf
mechanisms: popular narratives spread and mutate
narrative prevalence can affect economic behavior
epidemic models provide a quantitative analogy for narrative diffusion
objects.claim_boundary: Narrative diffusion is not a proven one-way causal law for prices; reverse causality and identification remain material concerns.

objects.title: Epidemics and Rumours
mechanisms: rumour spreaders can stop spreading after encounters with informed agents
crowding can create endogenous decay
objects.claim_boundary: Used as a saturation/crowding analogue, not as a direct market-pricing theorem.

objects.title: A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades
mechanisms: agents may rationally ignore private information after observing predecessors
cascades can form rapidly and remain fragile
objects.claim_boundary: Supports microfoundations for imitation/cascades; does not by itself identify narrative state in live markets.

objects.title: The Economics of Superstars
mechanisms: small differences can generate disproportionate market rewards
scale can concentrate earnings and market share
objects.claim_boundary: Explains concentration mechanisms, not ex-ante identification of future corporate superstars.

objects.title: Network Externalities, Competition, and Compatibility
mechanisms: product value can rise with network size
compatibility and installed base shape competition
objects.claim_boundary: Network effects are contingent on actual interoperability/adoption conditions; they are not presumed for every technology market.

objects.title: Competing Technologies, Increasing Returns, and Lock-In by Historical Events
mechanisms: increasing returns can amplify early advantages
path dependence can generate lock-in
objects.claim_boundary: Lock-in is a possible mechanism, not a universal property or guarantee of durable value capture.

objects.title: Do Stocks Outperform Treasury Bills?
mechanisms: long-run aggregate stock wealth creation is highly concentrated
cross-sectional outcomes are strongly right-skewed
objects.claim_boundary: Documents realized right-tail concentration; it does not prove investors can identify winners ex ante.

objects.title: Limiting forms of the frequency distribution of the largest or smallest member of a sample
objects.source_locator: Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 24(2):180-190
mechanisms: sample extremes have limiting distribution families distinct from center-of-distribution analysis
objects.claim_boundary: EVT characterizes statistical tails under assumptions; it does not explain structural business winners or guarantee tail predictability.

objects.title: The Variation of Certain Speculative Prices
mechanisms: price changes can exhibit heavy tails
Gaussian assumptions can understate extremes
objects.claim_boundary: Fat-tail evidence motivates robust tail analysis; it does not identify causal precursors of specific extreme events.

objects.title: The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities
mechanisms: nonlinear contingent-claim payoffs
option value depends on price, volatility, time and contract terms
objects.claim_boundary: Convex payoff is not free alpha; premium, volatility, time decay, liquidity and model assumptions remain binding.

objects.title: Theory of Rational Option Pricing
objects.source_locator: Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science 4(1):141-183
mechanisms: continuous-time contingent-claim valuation
state-contingent payoff replication
objects.claim_boundary: Supports payoff/price separation; R2 reverse-DCF use is an engineering expectations method, not a theorem from option pricing.

objects.title: Safety First and the Holding of Assets
mechanisms: portfolio choice can prioritize avoiding a disaster threshold
downside probability is a first-class constraint
objects.claim_boundary: Safety-first defines a constraint logic; production survival limits require portfolio-specific calibration.

objects.title: A New Interpretation of Information Rate
mechanisms: repeated favorable bets can be sized to maximize asymptotic log wealth
overbetting can damage geometric growth
objects.claim_boundary: Full Kelly is not a default investment rule under estimation error, fat tails, leverage or liquidity constraints.

objects.title: Optimal Gambling Systems for Favorable Games
objects.source_locator: Fourth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability
mechanisms: growth-optimal betting has strong long-run properties under known favorable games
objects.claim_boundary: Known-game assumptions are stronger than real investing; robust discounting is an engineering extension.

objects.title: Lifetime Portfolio Selection under Uncertainty: The Continuous-Time Case
mechanisms: dynamic portfolio choice links consumption, wealth and risky allocation through time
objects.claim_boundary: Continuous-time portfolio theory does not remove model uncertainty or practical liquidity constraints.

objects.title: Causal AI all-weather and extreme-event signal framework
objects.source_locator: user-provided 因果AI（To 潜在客户）(2)(1).pdf and 2026-01-24 interview notes
mechanisms: search for leading factors of extreme events
represent direction, strength and lag in risk transmission
estimate state-conditioned extreme-event probability and impact
objects.claim_boundary: Self-reported accuracy, returns and causal identification are not independently verified; R2 uses only the problem framing and requires PIT/OOS calibration before maturity promotion.
